UTN / Revel8 · Industry collaboration

MIME-aware phishing analysis

A parser-first pipeline for turning complex email content into structured model inputs and fine-grained phishing classifications.

The problem

MIME-formatted emails contain structure and content that must be processed before useful classification. The project addressed both preprocessing and the evaluation of fine-grained social-engineering categories.

What I built

In the UTN/Revel8 industry collaboration, I built a Python preprocessing and classification pipeline, extracted and normalized relevant email content, supported local and cloud-based LLM inference, applied prompt engineering with zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought approaches, and fine-tuned RoBERTa and EmoBERTa classifiers.

Technical approach

The parser-first design separates email processing from model inference. I compared prompting strategies and classifier-based approaches while evaluating intent, tactics, tools, and psychological triggers. Failure analysis was used to examine where each approach struggled.

Result & evidence

The resulting system combines structured preprocessing, multiple inference strategies, and fine-grained classification. The work included analyzing model failure cases and connecting data preparation and prompting choices with downstream prediction quality.
